title: Wharton Investment Competition — long-horizon non-comparable draft

applicability.notes: Season-specific client briefs, trading requirements, and deadlines should be pinned by a future season selector.

required_roles.title: student team leader and submitter
duties: Coordinate the team, own official communications, and submit required deliverables.

required_roles.title: investment strategy lead
duties: Translate the client's objectives and risk tolerance into a coherent investment policy.

required_roles.title: market and company research lead
duties: Gather public evidence, maintain citations, and challenge unsupported claims.

required_roles.title: portfolio and quantitative analyst
duties: Analyze trades, portfolio behavior, and consistency with the investment policy.

fill_role.title: report and presentation contributor
duties: Develop evidence-backed sections and improve the final report's clarity and defensibility.

turn_budget.derivation: A short agent run cannot reproduce a competition lasting more than ten weeks.

state_requirements.description: Teams share a WInS account and manage a portfolio through real market movement over the season.
Trading activity, interim work, and deliverables unfold across the published season schedule.
A registered educator may guide the team within official limits but may not trade or decide strategy.

internet.conditions: Research must use public information and may not contact the client.

code_execution.conditions: Analysis code may support research but cannot fabricate trades or market history.

generative_ai.conditions: AI may support brainstorming only; AI-derived material must be cited and may not be submitted as the team's own work.

constraints.statement: A team contains four to six students from the same school or campus and designates one student team leader.
The team shares one WInS account and places all official trades through it.
Generative AI may be used for brainstorming, but the team may not submit AI-generated work as its own and must cite AI-derived material.
constraints.waiver_reason: An LLM-agent benchmark necessarily uses generated analysis and prose as the submission.

constraints.statement: The draft evaluates a static case response without real trading, portfolio drift, or advisor interaction.

collaboration.notes: The student leader remains the official submission channel, while analytical responsibilities may rotate.

submission.official_deliverable: Investment Policy Statement and Comprehensive Final Report
submission.adaptation: The draft omits the live portfolio record and serializes the report as text.

evaluation.notes: Create and calibrate a benchmark rubric before treating automated scores as valid.

waivers.official_rule: Teams may not submit AI-generated work as their own.
waivers.benchmark_treatment: LLM agents generate the analysis and prose being evaluated.

waivers.official_rule: Teams trade and manage a portfolio over a live multi-week market period.
waivers.benchmark_treatment: The benchmark provides a static case and no live trading account.

sources.title: Wharton Investment Competition rules and roles
sources.locator: Team size, advisor, account, deliverable, and AI rules

provenance.notes: The current benchmark's team range and profile must be corrected before migration.
